name: Alan B. Bond
bio: Alan B. Bond is a Montclair, New Jersey resident running in NJ-11 under the Hope for Tomorrow label. He holds degrees from Dartmouth and Harvard Business School, worked at Morgan Guaranty, Goldman Sachs and W.R. Lazard, and later ran a pension management firm. He was convicted in a 2003 federal kickback case, served prison time until 2008 and paid restitution and fines.
notes: No published issue positions were found; Ballotpedia could not be retrieved. Instagram account found via search and not opened.

name: Adam Hamawy
bio: Adam Hamawy is a plastic and reconstructive surgeon based in Princeton who grew up in Old Bridge after emigrating from Egypt as an infant. He served as a combat trauma surgeon in the U.S. Army Medical Corps, retiring as a lieutenant colonel, and has done volunteer medical work in conflict zones including Gaza. He won the June 2026 Democratic primary for the open NJ-12 seat.

platform.point: Enact single-payer Medicare for All with no out-of-pocket costs, plus dental, vision and hearing coverage.
Negotiate drug prices, reform pharmacy benefit managers and cancel medical debt.
Write abortion rights into federal law and address racial gaps in maternal health.
Calls for abolishing ICE.
Supports a moratorium on new data centers.
Rejects corporate PAC money and lists fighting corruption as a priority.

economy.evidence: Campaign targets corporate consolidation, pharmacy middlemen and costs for working families.

welfare.evidence: Backs universal single-payer Medicare for All.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports codifying reproductive rights in federal law.

tech.evidence: Supports a moratorium on data centers.

education.evidence: Says he wants to restore strong public schools regardless of zip code.

notes: The Commons photo was taken from a congressional office's Instagram post, so it was not used as a portrait. Foreign-policy position (called Israel's actions in Gaza a genocide) not scored.

name: Gregg Mele
bio: Gregg Mele is a Plainfield, New Jersey attorney practicing corporate, securities, real estate and estate law who previously worked on Wall Street. He graduated from Montclair State and NYU Law School and teaches graduate courses at Stevens Institute. He has run for office several times before as an independent and a Libertarian and is the 2026 Republican nominee in NJ-12.

platform.point: Cut taxes and reduce government regulation.
Expand domestic energy production.
Expand school choice, including charter schools and education savings accounts.
Backs ICE enforcement and opposes sanctuary policies.
Build a competitive health care market with price transparency.
Proposes letting donors give to races rather than individual candidates.

economy.evidence: Favors tax cuts, less regulation, smaller government and free-market solutions.

welfare.evidence: Prefers a competitive health care market with price transparency.

immigration.evidence: Supports ICE operations and says sanctuary policies are not legal.

foreign.evidence: Calls U.S. action against Iran justified but opposes sending American ground troops.

education.evidence: Supports school choice, charter schools and parental rights.

name: Andres Jinete
bio: Andres Jinete is a Bound Brook, New Jersey resident and member of the Central Jersey Tenant Union. He studies management at Kean University and has about ten years of library experience. He is the Green Party nominee in NJ-12.

platform.point: Create a renters bill of rights and use a Housing First approach to homelessness.
Establish universal health care.
Cancel student debt and restore tuition-free college.
Opposes data centers outright, calling a moratorium insufficient.

economy.evidence: Backs a renters bill of rights and student debt cancellation.

welfare.evidence: Supports universal health care and tuition-free college.

tech.evidence: Opposes data centers entirely rather than a moratorium.

education.evidence: Calls for reinstating tuition-free public colleges.

name: Winston Jordan
bio: Winston Jordan is a Brooklyn native living in Hopewell Township, New Jersey. He is a U.S. Army veteran who worked as a computer systems analyst, engineer and IT executive in the pharmaceutical and tech sectors. A former Democrat, he runs an independent campaign that accepts no donations.

platform.point: Pass an American Economic Security Act with a $50,000 minimum livable income guarantee.
Offer a 50-year tax holiday for the bottom 99% of earners.
Supports Medicare for All.
Run a 24/7 digital town hall letting constituents vote on congressional decisions.
Supports the Stop Act to ban members of Congress from making fundraising calls.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All and a $50,000 guaranteed minimum income.

notes: Campaign site content could not be read in full.

name: Melanie Stansbury
bio: Melanie Stansbury has represented New Mexico's 1st district in the U.S. House since 2021, after serving in the New Mexico House from 2019 to 2021. Born in Farmington and raised in Albuquerque, she worked at the Office of Management and Budget, on the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee and as a consultant at Sandia National Laboratories. She holds degrees from Saint Mary's College of California and Cornell.

platform.point: Raise the federal minimum wage to $15 an hour.
Supports Medicare for All and coverage regardless of pre-existing conditions.
Modernize electric grids and invest in broadband, drinking water and roads.
Pass climate legislation and develop renewable energy.
Raise teacher pay and expand early childhood education, school meals and paid family leave.
Humane policies that reunite families and create a path to citizenship.

economy.evidence: Supports a $15 federal minimum wage and refuses corporate PAC money.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All and expanded paid family leave.

liberty.evidence: Abortion, LGBTQ rights and drugs: backs reproductive access, anti-discrimination and cannabis decriminalization; guns: pledged an assault weapons ban.

immigration.evidence: Backs family reunification and a path to citizenship.

energy.evidence: Calls for climate legislation and renewables; voted for the Inflation Reduction Act.

education.evidence: Wants higher teacher pay and expanded early childhood education.

name: Didi Okpareke
bio: Ndidiamaka "Didi" Okpareke is a Rio Rancho pharmacist who owns Olive Tree Compounding Pharmacy. She earned her pharmacy degree at UNM after attending Sandia High School. She is the 2026 Republican nominee in NM-1.

platform.point: Increase the number of health providers and keep rural pharmacies open.
Encourage entrepreneurship, investment and less state reliance on federal aid.
Address the state's low education rankings and high crime.
Willing to work with members across the aisle on solutions.

name: Gabe Vasquez
bio: Gabe Vasquez has represented New Mexico's 2nd district in the U.S. House since 2023 and sits on the Agriculture and Armed Services committees. Born in El Paso, he served on the Las Cruces City Council from 2017 to 2021. He previously worked in journalism, at the Las Cruces Hispanic Chamber of Commerce, as a staffer for Sen. Martin Heinrich and in conservation groups.

platform.point: Repeal Trump tax cuts for the wealthy, cut taxes for working families and pass the PRO Act.
Reverse health cuts, create a public option, cap insulin and let Medicare negotiate drug prices.
Crack down on cartels and smugglers and toughen penalties for fentanyl traffickers.
Fund border security, refocus ICE on violent criminals and give Dreamers a path to status.
Protect public lands access and oppose selling federal lands.
Oppose any federal ban on abortion or birth control.

economy.evidence: Wants to repeal tax cuts for the wealthy and supports the PRO Act.

welfare.evidence: Supports a public option and Medicare drug price negotiation; pledged to restore Medicaid and food aid cuts.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports codifying Roe; also backed a COVID vaccine requirement for health workers.

security.evidence: Raised the Las Cruces police budget and backs harsher penalties for traffickers and violent crime.

immigration.evidence: Backs border security funding while protecting Dreamers and opposing mass deportation.

energy.evidence: Supported pausing new oil and gas leases and a transition to renewables.

tech.evidence: Voted for the 2024 law forcing TikTok's divestment.

name: Greg Cunningham
current_role: Retired police detective and business owner
bio: Greg Cunningham is a lifelong New Mexican and Marine Corps reconnaissance veteran. He worked as an Albuquerque Police Department detective and later owned a private investigations business. He ran for the New Mexico House in 2022 and 2024 and is the 2026 Republican nominee in NM-2.

platform.point: Emphasizes law and order and holding people accountable for crimes.
Defends the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's Medicaid changes and wants to root out ineligible enrollment.
Promises commonsense, conservative-guided solutions that put people over politics.
Lists the economy, public safety, health care, education, energy and border security as focus areas.

welfare.evidence: Defends Medicaid changes in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and stresses eligibility checks.

notes: Campaign site lists issue areas without detailed proposals.

name: Teresa Leger Fernández
bio: Teresa Leger Fernández has represented New Mexico's 3rd district in the U.S. House since 2021 and chairs the Democratic Women's Caucus. Born in Las Vegas, New Mexico, she practiced law in Santa Fe for about 30 years, focusing on community development, tribal advocacy and civil rights. She was a White House Fellow and served on the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation, and holds degrees from Yale and Stanford Law School.

platform.point: Affordable, quality health care close to home for all Americans.
Protect families and communities from gun violence.
Seeks humane, comprehensive immigration reform.
Protect land, air and water for future generations.
Defend voting rights and strengthen democratic institutions.
Support tribal self-determination.

economy.evidence: Supports a New Mexico Green New Deal.

liberty.evidence: Guns: supports banning military-style semi-automatic rifles.

immigration.evidence: Backs comprehensive reform and the DREAM Act.

energy.evidence: Advocates moving from fracking to clean energy under a Green New Deal.

name: Martin Zamora
bio: Martin R. Zamora has represented District 63 in the New Mexico House of Representatives since 2019. Born and raised near Clovis, he owns and operates farming and ranching businesses in Curry and Torrance counties. He is the 2026 Republican nominee in NM-3.

platform.point: Defend private property and water rights and cut federal rules on producers.
Lower taxes, reduce red tape and support small businesses.
Back sheriffs and law enforcement and treat fentanyl trafficking as a national emergency.
Secure the southern border and end sanctuary policies.

economy.evidence: Calls for lower taxes, less red tape and fewer federal regulations.

security.evidence: Wants closer work with local law enforcement and a fentanyl national emergency.

immigration.evidence: Calls for border security and ending sanctuary policies.

notes: Crime and border details were confirmed on the campaign site's issue pages.

name: Nick LaLota
bio: Nick LaLota has represented New York's 1st district in the U.S. House since 2023 and sits on the Appropriations and Small Business committees. A Long Island native and Naval Academy graduate, he served as a Navy officer with three overseas deployments. He later earned an MBA and law degree from Hofstra, served as an Amityville village trustee and worked in Suffolk County government.

platform.point: Cut taxes and restore state and local tax (SALT) deduction relief.
Strengthen border and immigration enforcement.
Support law enforcement.
Pursue peace through strength.
Protect Long Island water quality and secure federal funds for local projects.

economy.evidence: Campaign prioritizes tax cuts and SALT relief and contrasts freedom with socialism.

liberty.evidence: LGBTQ: opposes bans on same-sex marriage.

immigration.evidence: Cosponsored the DIGNIDAD Act pairing legal status with tighter border enforcement.
